seed_question: Open questions in quantum foundations and in Heron r2 device physics that fit the IBM Open Plan (600 QPU s/month, 374 s left, project hard stop 420 s), with the quantum chip as ground truth, never as a computational resource.

qpu.cost_rule: 0.28 ms x shots + ~2 s/job; x1.5 for mid-circuit measurement

directions.title: Does a correctly scheduled noise model close the Stage 1 gap?
directions.assumption_at_stake: The Stage 1 gap is the device departing from its calibration, not our simulator mis-built
directions.cheapest_test: Re-simulate the archived ISA circuit ALAP-scheduled (FakeFez durations) with job-time calibration; pass if P(yes) >= 0.40
directions.rules_out: Rules out our simulator's missing idle decay as the cause of the 3 November gap: scheduling the circuit correctly moved the prediction by about 0.000 (0.268 against 0.267).

directions.title: Coherent or stochastic? Twirling and DD on the Stage 1 circuit
directions.assumption_at_stake: Reported (twirled) error rates describe an untwirled structured circuit
directions.cheapest_test: 4 interleaved arms x 2,000 shots (as run / twirl / DD XY4 / both) + readout cal; pass if twirl moves P(yes) >= 0.125 toward the corrected sim at >= 3 sigma
directions.rules_out: Rules out nothing about twirling: the 3 November gap was absent on 4 November (0.246 against 0.269), so there was nothing to close; it set the defaults (twirl off, DD off).

directions.title: Is the gap nine particular qubits, or one afternoon?
directions.assumption_at_stake: The gap is a stable property of the device as calibrated
directions.cheapest_test: 2 pre-chosen alternative layouts x 2,000 shots + 2 repeats >= 3 h apart; pass if both alternative-layout gaps < half the same-job original gap
directions.rules_out: Rules out nothing about bad qubits: with no gap on 4 November, both alternative layouts also sat near the simulator (0.277 and 0.297 against 0.265 and 0.264).

directions.title: Does DD restore the missing entanglement?
directions.assumption_at_stake: The missing witness negativity is idle dephasing
directions.cheapest_test: Re-tomography of item h088, DD off vs XY4, 1,000 shots/setting; pass if DD raises negativity by >= 0.043 with 95% CI above 0

directions.title: Coherent or incoherent, from the archived tomography
directions.assumption_at_stake: Reported (twirled) error rates describe untwirled circuits
directions.cheapest_test: 7-parameter coherent (local unitaries + ZZ) vs incoherent (local Pauli + depolarising) fits to 3 archived tomographies; pass if coherent wins by dlogL >= 10 on >= 2 of 3
directions.rules_out: Rules out, on program 1's three archived pairs, a pure steady-twist account winning a 7-against-7 fit; the contest was decided by the reference state's purity, so P3-5c re-asked it (pass).

directions.title: Does ibm_fez leak settings between qubits?
directions.assumption_at_stake: On-chip no-signalling holds on this Heron r2
directions.cheapest_test: Rybotycki idle test on ~40 pairs, phase-only settings; pass (clean) if no |dP| > 4.5 sigma after Bonferroni

directions.title: Two-friend genuine local friendliness with external settings
directions.assumption_at_stake: Local friendliness (absoluteness of observed events + no superdeterminism + locality)
directions.cheapest_test: Bong facet 1, 3x3 settings, friend n = 0,1,2,4, 2,500 shots/setting, beacon-fixed settings, decohered-friend and no-signalling controls; pass if S > 0 by >= 5 sigma at some n >= 1 with controls passing

directions.title: Is there a one-friend genuine LF inequality?
directions.assumption_at_stake: For one friend there are no genuine LF inequalities beyond Bell
directions.cheapest_test: Facet enumeration + see-saw of the one-friend 3-setting LF polytope; pass if a non-Bell facet with >= 15% white-noise tolerance exists

directions.title: Sequential Peres-Mermin under exact Contextuality-by-Default
directions.assumption_at_stake: Program 1's CbD pipeline sees contextuality where it exists; PM contextuality survives exact CbD on superconducting hardware
directions.cheapest_test: 24 MCM circuits (6 contexts x 2 orders x 2 states) x 4,000 shots, individual outcomes; pass if exact CbD LP rejects noncontextuality (CNT2 99% lower bound > 0) for both states

directions.title: Sequential 4-cycle with the exact KDL criterion
directions.assumption_at_stake: Program 1's CbD pipeline sees contextuality where it exists (cyclic case)
directions.cheapest_test: 8 MCM circuits x 4,000 shots; pass if KDL statistic > 2 with 99.9% lower bound > 2 in both orders

directions.title: Leggett-Garg with MCM, clumsiness control and CbD
directions.assumption_at_stake: Macrorealism with noninvasive measurability for one transmon; 'IBM violations are clumsiness'
directions.cheapest_test: 16 circuits x 4,000 shots x 6 parallel copies; pass if CbD-corrected K3 > 1 by >= 5 sigma and K3 - 1 exceeds classical-preparation disturbance by >= 3 sigma

directions.title: Do alternating non-commuting measurements show memory?
directions.assumption_at_stake: No superdeterministic memory at microsecond spacing
directions.cheapest_test: ~50 qubits, 8 alternating Z/X MCMs + all-Z control, 2 x 4,000 shots; pass if |Corr| < 0.01 at lags 2, 4, 6 and control repeat agreement >= 95%

directions.title: LG-certified randomness from P3-11's data
directions.assumption_at_stake: One transmon's LG violation certifies randomness semi-device-independently
directions.cheapest_test: Nath Theorem 2 bound with finite-size correction on P3-11's mixed-preparation data; pass if >= 0.05 bits/round at 99%

directions.title: Maximally psi-epistemic models in d = 4, no fair sampling
directions.cheapest_test: Two-transmon real-amplitude ququart, 30 circuits x 2,000 shots + tomography; pass if S + 5 sigma < 1 under both omega_q choices

directions.title: What made 3 November different: the afternoon, or the circuit's barrier and shot grouping?
directions.assumption_at_stake: Program 1's 3 November gap was the chip that afternoon, not the circuit's barrier or its one-block shot grouping
directions.cheapest_test: {barrier, no barrier} x {one 1,000-shot block, 10 x 100 interleaved} + R0/R1 on the original nine qubits; repeated >= 3 h later; pass if the barrier block gives P(yes) >= 0.40 and beats the no-barrier block by >= 0.10 at z >= 3 in job 1
directions.rules_out: Rules out the pre-measurement barrier and the shot grouping as the cause of 3 November's 0.50: every arm in two runs gave 0.27-0.32.

directions.title: Does 3 November's result come back when the circuit runs alone in its own job?
directions.assumption_at_stake: Program 1's 3 November gap was the chip that afternoon, not the circuit running alone in its own job
directions.cheapest_test: (A) barrier circuit alone in its own job, (B) no-barrier circuit alone, (C) both in one job; 1,000 shots each on the original nine qubits, back to back in a seeded order; pass if A gives P(yes) >= 0.40 and beats C's barrier circuit by >= 0.10 at z >= 3

directions.question: What made 3 November different? (program 1's Stage 1 gap: the chip said yes 50% of the time, its simulator 25%)
directions.closing_diagnosis: If P3-16 misses, the question closes: the corrected simulator (P3-1), same-day reruns on three layouts (P3-2, P3-3), the barrier and the shot grouping (P3-15) and the lone job (P3-16) are everything about the circuit, simulator and job that we control, and every run since 3 November gave 0.25-0.32. The 0.50 was that afternoon's chip, not reproducible and not a property of our set-up. No more chip seconds go to it.
directions.if_pass: If P3-16 passes, the question stays open with one follow-up only: the lone-job run repeated on another day (invariant 7), before anything is claimed about job scheduling.

directions.short: Readout error as the blur term?
directions.title: Can extra readout error stand in for P3-5c's blur term?
directions.assumption_at_stake: The blur-type term P3-5c needed is error in the chip's state, not readout error beyond the job's own calibration.
directions.cheapest_test: Refit P3-5c's models on the archive with four readout knobs per pair, bounded at 3x the binomial error of the job's own calibration; parametric bootstrap as P3-5c. Design files already being prepared by another session (experiments/p3_17_readout.py, uncommitted at remap time).
directions.models: none: archived chip data, no model (rule 12 does not apply)
directions.odds_event: With readout knobs bounded at 3x each job's calibration error, the blur-type term is still needed (p < 0.01) on all three archived pairs. (Remap draft; if P3-17's pre-registration states a different event, it logs the change and both odds stay.)
directions.odds_rationale: The ng-p3-5c audit found readout can absorb blur on h221 and h268 only with knobs of 2.7-5% per qubit, 3-20 times IBM's reported error; 3x the calibration's own binomial error is far tighter. Risk: h088 already misfits, and tight bounds may still help on the weakest pair. Above the running base rate 8/19 = 0.42 (ledger/brier.md); program 3 is 0 hits in 4 scored.

known: A refit found the saved chip data need both a 'rotation' and a 'blur' kind of error term on all three pairs.
The auditor found readout errors could fake the blur, but only if they were several times bigger than IBM reports.

Will it come back a hit (here, a hit means the blur is still needed when misreading is allowed for)?

directions.short: Both error terms on a fresh run?
directions.title: Do both error terms show up again when the three entangled pairs are measured in a fresh chip job?
directions.assumption_at_stake: P3-5c's 'both terms on every pair' describes the chip, not one afternoon's job.
directions.cheapest_test: One new job: program 1's three witness circuits on their original qubits, 9 tomography settings x 2,000 shots each, plus readout calibration; P3-5c's fits, unchanged.
directions.models: none: the chip is the referee, no model (rule 12 does not apply)
directions.odds_event: On the fresh job, the 16-knob model needs both the rotation-type and the blur-type term (each p < 0.01) on at least 2 of the 3 pairs.
directions.odds_rationale: Invariant 7: P3-5c is pass-unreplicated. Both kinds of error are generic on superconducting chips, so a second job should need both; but half the shots widen the nulls, calibration drifts between days (P3-15's runs), and h221's rotation label was the weakest. Above the running base rate 8/19 = 0.42 (ledger/brier.md).
